Synopsis:
    A Capgemini survey of 1,300 large organisations across 11 countries finds that digital infrastructure resilience is rising to board level, driven by geopolitical tensions, export controls and cyber threats. Organisations are treating digital infrastructure like physical supply chains, prioritising substitutability of critical providers, data sovereignty and control over AI/data assets. Replacement timelines for critical providers are long — often exceeding a year — pushing firms toward retaining control of key workloads rather than outright vendor replacement.
